name: French Guiana

findings.local_actor: SPLANG (86.5% owned by Collectivité Territoriale de Guyane)
findings.financier: EU (FEDER, CEF Digital Gateways), CNES, AFD loan
findings.summary: Lum@link, a roughly 2,000 km public submarine cable from Cayenne to EllaLink's system off Fortaleza, Brazil, owned by the territory's SPLANG, about EUR 75.8m, EU/AFD/CNES-financed, under construction with commissioning targeted for December 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller convention: GUF is coded as its own territory, so French-state, French-company and EU controllers are 'third', not 'domestic'; only Guianese actors (CTG, SPLANG) are domestic. Equipment rule: wet-plant supplier not named in opened sources; EllaLink is documented as builder and operator, so it is treated as controller (third). Owner SPLANG is domestic. Tier 4: financing closed and construction under way (AFD start 1 July 2025); tier 5 once commissioned. EUR values not converted, so USD null. Intended to replace the ageing Americas II cable.

findings.summary: Orange inaugurated Kanawa, a self-funded EUR 35m submarine fibre cable of about 1,750 km linking French Guiana with Martinique, with commercial service planned from end-January 2019.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller convention: GUF is coded as its own territory, so French-state, French-company and EU controllers are 'third', not 'domestic'; only Guianese actors (CTG, SPLANG) are domestic. Equipment vendor not named, so the documented owner-operator Orange (France) is treated as controller. Both sources likely relay the same Orange announcement, weakening independence. Pre-2020 and current operation not confirmed in this run, so still_current null. Sources differ on length (1,746 vs 1,766 km).

findings.summary: Orange began 5G service in Cayenne and Rémire-Montjoly on 1 August 2023 after Arcep granted 700 MHz and 3.4-3.8 GHz licences; Digicel AFG, Free Caraïbe and Outremer Telecom were also licensed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the radio-equipment vendor for Orange's Guiana 5G network is not named in the opened source, and the equipment rule makes the vendor the controller. Tier 4 because only an initial-area rollout is documented.

findings.local_actor: SPLANG on behalf of Collectivité Territoriale de Guyane
findings.summary: SPLANG tendered a feasibility study on algorithmic video surveillance for schools, territorial aerodromes and CTG administrative sites, with a final roadmap due November 2024; no software vendor was named.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null because no vendor or stack is identified; this is a study, not a deployment. Outcome of the study and any subsequent procurement unknown.

facilities.null_reason: two searches returned only aggregator listings of small colocation sites (Wayscom, Guyane Numérique) and results about Guyana; no large data-centre project with an identifiable owner-operator

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase or export-licence item surfaced in other searches

models.null_reason: one search found no CTG or territorial partnership with any model provider and no local model

research_gaps: Radio/core equipment vendors of Orange Caraïbe, Digicel AFG, SFR Caraïbe/Outremer Telecom and Free Caraïbe in French Guiana, and whether any Huawei kit there falls under France's 2019 high-risk-vendor authorisation regime and its 2028 removal deadlines.
Wet-plant supplier of Lum@link and whether it was commissioned by December 2026.
Equipment supplier of the Kanawa cable and the Americas II cable's status.
Outcome of SPLANG's 2024 algorithmic video-surveillance feasibility study and any subsequent procurement and vendor.
Vendors of municipal CCTV in Cayenne, Kourou and Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni.
